notes: Payroll is out of scope: jurisdiction-specific and explicitly not portable. Leave and attendance are the MVP surface. The render set is a vendored Compose project — the application plus the MariaDB service the installer needs — and the application image is built from that tree's Dockerfile (php:8.3-apache-bookworm, release archive from SourceForge with its MD5 verified at build time), because upstream publishes no image. The service declares its own `build:`, so the deployment builds the image on this host from that tree during the `build` stage and runs it from the local store: it is never pushed and never pulled — `pull_policy: never` makes an absent image an error instead of a download, and the tag lives in the platform's own namespace (`seamnex/orangehrm:5.9`) so a reference under the product's name can never resolve to a third party's repackaging, which is how an uninstalled application once ran under this entry's tag. Identity is per instance: the id the build produced is recorded on the first deploy and compared on later ones, which makes the `imageDigest` above reference data rather than the enforced pin. Nothing about the install is left to a browser: the entrypoint waits for the database, installs once with the values this catalog declares once an operator has accepted the product's licence (`ORANGEHRM_INSTALLER_LICENSE_AGREED`, default false), and hands lib/confs, src/cache, src/log and src/config back to www-data. `lib/confs/Conf.php` is the marker, so a restart never reinstalls. Two volumes are worth backing up: orangehrm-conf (Conf.php, and the data-encryption key when enabled) and orangehrm-db (/var/lib/mysql, the schema itself). OrangeHRM Starter has no OIDC or SAML and reads no identity headers, so identity is gate-only: the edge protects the route and the product keeps its own login, which an operator provisions outside the platform. Its REST API is served under /web/index.php/api/v2/<module>; /api is not an OrangeHRM path. The silent installer stores neither a default language nor a timezone, so the product's own defaults apply until an administrator changes them in the UI — which is why those two variables are not offered.
deviation: Upstream ships a Dockerfile, no Compose file and no image at all, so the render set is vendored: docker-compose.yml with the application and a mariadb:11.4 service, plus a Dockerfile that reproduces upstream's build and adds the first-boot install. Six deliberate changes to upstream, recorded row by row in platform/upstream/D07-01/README.md: (1) the database service is added — the installer cannot run without one, and it *refuses* a database that already exists, which is why MARIADB_DATABASE is not set; (2) upstream's `VOLUME ["/var/www/html"]` is removed, because it would shadow the installed tree with an empty anonymous volume on first run and present an uninstalled product after every restart; (3) the install runs at boot instead of in a browser, through the deprecated `installer/cli_install.php`, because its replacement (`installer/console install:on-new-database`) refuses to run without a TTY; (4) `HTTPS` is derived from the edge's `X-Forwarded-Proto`, because the edge terminates TLS and the product otherwise emits every absolute URL as `http://`; (5) the service declares `build:` under `pull_policy: never` and a tag in the platform's own namespace, so the deployment builds the image from this tree in its `build` stage and runs it locally — never published, never fetched; a tag under the product's name could only ever resolve to a third party's repackaging, and the build id recorded per instance is what a later deploy is compared against; (6) the image states its licence in OCI labels and carries `IMAGE-LICENCES.md`, which names the product's licence as an unverified reference rather than asserting one the archive has not been read for. Nothing in the tree patches the product: a modified PHP file would make the image a modified version under GPL-3.0 §5 and break the MD5-verified 'unmodified archive' claim.
